name: Symbolic-Compiled Decoupled Architecture
summary: Separate high-level symbolic natural language parsing from low-level compiled hardware execution routines to ensure both flexible reasoning and deterministic low-latency control.
steps: Parse natural language intents into structured logical representations or ASTs using a high-level symbolic engine (e.g., Lisp or LLM router).
Implement latency-sensitive hardware drivers, telemetry monitors, and safety loops in compiled low-level languages like C or C++.
Establish inter-process communication (IPC) or bridge protocols between the high-level symbolic reasoning layer and low-level execution binaries.
jarvis_use: Decouple high-level voice decision-making from low-level macOS system calls and device control scripts.

name: Model Context Protocol Server Wrappers
summary: Wrap local and remote data stores, filesystems, and APIs as MCP servers to expose standardized context and tools to autonomous agents.
steps: Deploy specialized MCP server endpoints for specific resources (e.g., Filesystem MCP, PostgreSQL MCP, Google Drive MCP, Slack MCP).
Configure security and policy guardrails using gateway components like GitHub MCP Guard.
Expose standardized tool schemas via MCP SDK or FastMCP for agent consumption.
jarvis_use: Provide JARVIS agent nodes with secure, standardized access to local files, databases, and third-party APIs.

name: Multi-Agent Graph Orchestration
summary: Structure complex AI assistant tasks into graph-based multi-agent workflows with specialized retrieval, security, and execution nodes.
steps: Define agent state graphs and task delegation logic using frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, or AutoGen.
Integrate retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines powered by LangChain, LlamaIndex, or DSPy.
Route agent outputs through security guardrails before tool invocation.
jarvis_use: Orchestrate multi-step task planning across specialized sub-agents inside JARVIS.

name: Symbolic AI Rule Engine
summary: Implement natural language understanding and logical inference using recursive list processing and explicit rule trees without neural network weights.
steps: Represent concepts, relationships, and natural language grammars as symbolic tree structures.
Write recursive functions and macro expansions to parse user inputs into executable logical queries.
Evaluate knowledge trees against structured world models to determine system actions.
jarvis_use: Provide explicit, deterministic command parsing and knowledge retrieval without relying on statistical LLM hallucinations.

name: Low-Latency Real-Time Hardware Control Loop
summary: Build non-blocking system drivers in compiled languages to handle real-time sensor processing and hardware control without garbage-collection pauses.
steps: Write modular hardware integration logic using C or C++ with direct memory access.
Implement real-time loop execution for telemetry reading, power management, and device control.
Expose high-speed control functions to IPC interfaces for consumption by high-level UI shells.
jarvis_use: Maintain low-latency system telemetry monitoring and hardware execution loops on host machines.

name: Polyglot Home Assistant Service Stack
summary: Architect a home assistant by combining web backends, device scripting, and mobile native bridges across multiple existing language ecosystems.
steps: Deploy a web service infrastructure layer (e.g., PHP web app logic).
Write device orchestration and automation scripts in Python.
Build native mobile frontend UI integrations in Objective-C.
jarvis_use: Connect JARVIS backends to local iOS/macOS client interfaces and legacy web endpoints.

name: Task-Specific Open LLM Routing Engine
summary: Route distinct assistant queries to open-source foundation models specialized for code generation, translation, or general instruction following.
steps: Maintain a catalog of task-specialized open-weight models (e.g., Qwen3-Coder for coding, Cohere Command for translation, Llama 3.1 for general reasoning).
Classify incoming user prompts by intent and required context length.
Dispatch queries to the appropriate specialized open model endpoint.
jarvis_use: Dynamically select optimal local/hosted open models based on prompt domain (coding vs reasoning vs translation).
